title: In the Workplace
goals: Make polite requests and ask for permission with could, would, may and would you mind.
Report what people told or asked you to do with told me to / asked me to.
Give advice and talk about possibility and necessity with should, could, might, have to and must.

learn.title: Polite requests and asking for permission
learn.html:
At work we often ask people to do something, or we ask if we can do something. Polite language is very important with customers and supervisors.

UseStructureExample
Ask someone to do somethingCould / Would / Can you + base verb?Could you help me with this order, please?
Ask someone to do something (very polite)Would you mind + verb-ing?Would you mind waiting a moment?
Ask for permissionMay / Could / Can I + base verb?May I leave early today?
Ask for permission (polite)Do you mind if I + present? / Would you mind if I + past?Do you mind if I open the window?
  • May is the most formal. Can is the most informal. Could is in the middle.
  • To say yes to Would you mind...? or Do you mind...?, say No, not at all or No, go ahead.
  • Do not use May you...? to ask other people to do something.

watch.wrong: Would you mind to wait a moment?
watch.right: Would you mind waiting a moment?
watch.why: After Would you mind, use verb + -ing.

watch.wrong: May you give me the invoice?
watch.right: Could you give me the invoice?
watch.why: May is for asking permission for yourself (May I...?), not for asking others.
After could, use the base verb without to.

watch.wrong: Do you mind if I opened the window?
watch.right: Do you mind if I open the window?
watch.why: After Do you mind if, use the present; with Would you mind if, use the past.

learn.title: Reported commands and requests: told me to / asked me to
learn.html:
We use told and asked to report what a person ordered or requested. Use told for commands and asked for polite requests.

What the person saidReported
"Call the client."My boss told me to call the client.
"Could you send the report, please?"She asked me to send the report.
"Don't be late."He told me not to be late.
"Please don't use your phone."They asked us not to use our phones.
  • Structure: told / asked + person + (not) to + base verb.
  • The person is always necessary: She told me to wait, not She told to wait.
  • Pronouns and possessives can change: "Send me your file" becomes She asked me to send her my file.

watch.wrong: The manager said me to close the store.
watch.right: The manager told me to close the store.
watch.why: Use told + person + to. Do not use said + person + to.

watch.wrong: He told me don't use the printer.
watch.right: He told me not to use the printer.
watch.why: A negative command is reported with not to + base verb.

watch.wrong: She asked me closing the door.
watch.right: She asked me to close the door.
watch.why: After asked me, use to + base verb.

watch.wrong: My boss told that I call the client.
watch.right: My boss told me to call the client.
watch.why: You need a person (me) and to + verb.

learn.title: Advice, suggestions, possibility and necessity
learn.html:
Modal verbs help us give advice, make suggestions, talk about possibility, and say what is necessary at work. They are followed by the base verb.

MeaningModalExample
Adviceshould / shouldn'tYou should talk to your supervisor.
SuggestioncouldYou could ask a colleague for help.
Possibilitymight / couldThe shipment might arrive tomorrow.
Necessity (rule)must / have toEmployees must wear a badge.
Not necessarydon't have toYou don't have to come on Sunday.
Prohibitedmustn'tYou mustn't smoke in the warehouse.
  • Must and have to are similar, but don't have to and mustn't are very different.
  • Have to changes: She has to, Does he have to...? Must never changes.

watch.wrong: She must to wear a uniform.
watch.why: After must, use the base verb without to.
The negative of must is mustn't (prohibited).

watch.wrong: He should to call the customer.
watch.why: After should, use the base verb without to.

watch.wrong: You mustn't come on Sunday. It's optional.
watch.right: You don't have to come on Sunday. It's optional.
watch.why: Mustn't means prohibited. Don't have to means it is not necessary.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• How can I help you? / What seems to be the problem? — starting with a customer.
  • I'm sorry for the trouble. / I apologize for the mistake. — apologizing.
  • Could you hold for a moment, please? — asking a customer to wait.
  • Let me see what I can do. / I'll solve it right away. — offering help.
  • Would you mind telling me your order number? — asking for information politely.
  • I understand how you feel. — showing you care.
  • Thank you for telling me. I'll try to do better. — answering criticism.
  • Can you give me an example? — asking for clear feedback.

write.model:
Subject: Request to change my schedule next week

Dear Mr. Ramos,

I hope you are well. I am writing to ask about my schedule next week. My daughter has a school event on Wednesday afternoon, and I would like to attend it. Would you mind if I left at two o'clock that day? I could come in earlier on Wednesday morning, or I could work two extra hours on Thursday.

Last week you told me to finish the monthly report by Friday, and I sent it on Thursday. You also asked me to train the new employee, and I have already started. I think I should finish both tasks on time, even with this change.

Could you please tell me if this is possible? I must tell my family by Monday, so I would be grateful for your answer before then.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Elena Torres

reading.title: How to handle criticism at work
paragraphs: Nobody likes to hear that their work is not perfect. However, criticism is a normal part of every job, and learning to handle it can help your career. Here is the story of Marta, a customer service agent in a call center in Guadalajara.

Last month, Marta's supervisor listened to some of her calls. After that, he asked her to come to his office. At first, Marta was very nervous. She thought, "Maybe I'm in trouble." Then he said, "You are very polite with customers, and they like you. But you should speak more slowly, and you could use simpler words. Would you mind practicing with a colleague this week?"

Marta felt a little hurt. She wanted to say, "I always do my best!" But she took a deep breath and said, "Thank you for telling me. I will try." Later that day, she asked her friend Luis to listen to her calls. He told her to smile when she spoke, because customers can hear it in your voice. He also told her not to use long sentences.

After two weeks, Marta's customers gave her better scores. Her supervisor told her that she had improved a lot. "You might become a team leader one day," he said. Marta was surprised, but very happy. She understood that her supervisor was not attacking her. He was helping her to grow, and now she thanks him often.

Experts say there are some simple steps to handle criticism well. First, you should listen carefully and not interrupt. Second, you must stay calm, even if you disagree. You don't have to accept every comment, but you should think about it. Third, you could ask a question, for example, "Can you give me an example?" Finally, make a plan to improve and thank the person. Remember: criticism is not an attack. It is information that can help you grow.

listening.title: A call about a broken machine
listening.intro: Listen to the phone call. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Good afternoon, Fresh Home Store. This is Dana. How can I help you?
Hello. I bought a washing machine last week, and it doesn't work. I'm very upset.
I'm sorry to hear that, sir. Would you mind telling me your order number?
Of course. It's four, seven, two, nine, one.
Thank you. Could you hold for a moment, please? I need to check something.
Sure, but please hurry. I have to leave for work in ten minutes.
I see the problem. A technician should visit you, but the next free day is Friday. Would that be OK?
No, I can't wait until Friday. I want a refund.
I understand. May I ask my supervisor? She told me to ask her about refunds.
Hello, sir. This is Mrs. Lopez. I'm sorry for the trouble. We can send a new machine tomorrow, or you can have a full refund.
A refund, please. You don't have to send another one.
No problem. You must return the machine first. Dana will email you the instructions. Is there anything else?
No, that's all. Thank you for your help.
Thank you for calling, sir. Have a nice day.
